# Preprocessing part 1: create Seurat object

We defined this function that create a Seurat object from 10X sample (filtered_bc_feature_matrix/). It also includes data normalization, scaling and also HTO demultiplexing. The output of this function is that it stores a Seurat RDS object that contains all the cells for later analysis.
```{r create Seurat object from 10X sample, eval=FALSE}
create_Seurat_RDS_from_10X_sample(sample_name, input_data_dir, all_cells_path)
```


# Preprocessing part 2_1: HTO Visualization {.tabset .tabset-fade}

After creating the Seurat object, we used various diagnostic plots to determine whether the data looks good, specifically HTO demultiplexing results.
```{r Read in the r object}
# read in the r object
Sample <- readRDS(all_cells_path)
```


Below are different visualizations (diagnostic plots) for the demultiplexing results. We used these visualizations to help us validate the demultiplexing results.

## Ridge plots

Ridge plots: Since each cell get assigned to one of the hashtags (two hashtags if it passes two hashtags' threshold - these cells are considered as doublets). Cells should have high expression with its corresponding assigned hashtag
```{r HTO - Demultiplexing Visualizations 1 - ridge plots, results='hide'}
# visualize enrichment for selected HTOs with ridge plots
# group cells based on the max HTO signal
Idents(Sample) <- "HTO_maxID"
num_hashtag <- length(row.names(Sample[["HTO"]]))

for(i in 1:num_hashtag){
  print(RidgePlot(Sample,assay="HTO",features=row.names(Sample[["HTO"]])[i]))
}
```

## Feature Scatter plots

In this section, we will visualize pairs of HTO signals to confirm mutual exclusivity in singlets.
We would expect dots are all near the axis instead of in the center which suggests high expression level in both hashtags.
- colors represent the assigned cell category: singlets or doublets or negative
```{r HTO - Demultiplexing Results Visualizations 2 - feature scatter plots}
DefaultAssay(Sample) <- "HTO"
Idents(Sample) <- "HTO_classification.global"

num_hashtag <- length(row.names(Sample[["HTO"]]))

for(i in 1:(num_hashtag-1)){
  print(FeatureScatter(Sample, feature1=row.names(Sample[["HTO"]])[i],feature2=row.names(Sample[["HTO"]])[i+1]))
}
```

## Violin plots for counts and features
In this section, we will compare number of UMIs for singlets, doublets, and negative cells. 
```{r HTO - Demultiplexing Results Visualizations 3 - Violin plots for counts and features}

Idents(Sample) <- "HTO_classification.global"
VlnPlot(Sample,features="nCount_RNA",pt.size=0.01,log=TRUE)
VlnPlot(Sample,features="nFeature_RNA",pt.size=0.01,log=TRUE)
#VlnPlot(Sample,features=c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA"), pt.size = 0.01, ncol=2)
```
## tSNE plot

In this section, we will generate a two dimensional tSNE embedding for HTOs. Here we are grouping cells by singlets and doublets.
We would expect Singlets to form clusters and doublets locates between singlet clusters.
```{r HTO - Demultiplexing Results Visualizations 4 - tSNE plot with singlets and doublets as lebales, results='hide', message=FALSE}

#Remove the negative cells from the object
Sample_non_negative <- subset(Sample, idents="Negative",invert=TRUE)
#Calculate w tSNE embedding of the HTO data
DefaultAssay(Sample_non_negative) <- "HTO"
Sample_non_negative <- ScaleData(Sample_non_negative,features=rownames(Sample_non_negative),verbose=FALSE)
Sample_non_negative <- RunPCA(Sample_non_negative,features=rownames(Sample_non_negative),approx=FALSE)
Sample_non_negative <- RunTSNE(Sample_non_negative,dims=1:7,perplexity=100, check_duplicates=FALSE) # takes a few minutes
DimPlot(Sample_non_negative,reduction="tsne")
```

Here is the tSNE plot with HTO hashtags as labels
```{r HTO - Demultiplexing Results Visualizations 5 - tSNE with HTO hashtags as labels}
Idents(Sample_non_negative) <- "HTO_classification"
DimPlot(Sample_non_negative, repel=TRUE) + NoLegend()
```

## HTO heatmap
HTO heatmap: visualize the expression of each cell for each hashtag
We want to keep those cells only shows high expression (yellow) in one of the hashtags (singlets)
```{r HTO - Demultiplexing Results Visualizations 6 - HTO heatmap}
HTOHeatmap(Sample_non_negative, assay="HTO")
```

## Summary

```{r tabularize number of cells per classification}
# Visualize number of cells per classification (singlets, doublets, negative)
table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)
n_doublet <- table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)[[1]]
n_negative <- table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)[[2]]
n_singlet <- table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)[[3]]
prop_singlet <- n_singlet/(n_doublet + n_negative + n_singlet)
print(paste("The proportion of singlets to total cells is: ", prop_singlet))
```

Now we can subset the singlets for further QC filtering.

```{r Extract Singlets}
# Extract Singlets 
DefaultAssay(Sample)<-"RNA"
Idents(Sample)<- "HTO_classification.global"
Sample.singlet<-subset(Sample, idents= "Singlet")
# get reads that map to the mitochondrial genome because low-quality/dying cells often exhibit extensive mitochondrial contamination
Sample.singlet[["percent.mt"]]<-PercentageFeatureSet(Sample.singlet, pattern = "^MT")
```

# Preprocessing part 3: QC filtering

Based on the above plots, perform QC filtering based on custom QC cutoffs
```{r QC - Define QC cutoffs}
# QC cutoffs defined by user

QC_nFeature_RNA_min <- 500
QC_nFeature_RNA_max <- 7500
QC_nCount_RNA_min <- 1500
QC_nCount_RNA_max <- 30000 
QC_percent_mt_max <- 10.0
```


```{r QC - filter out low quality cells}
# Perform QC filtering based on the custom QC cutoffs
# comment out the cutoffs that you don't want to use
Sample_filtered.singlet <- subset(Sample.singlet, 
                                  subset = nFeature_RNA > QC_nFeature_RNA_min & 
                                    nFeature_RNA < QC_nFeature_RNA_max & 
                                    nCount_RNA > QC_nCount_RNA_min & 
                                    nCount_RNA < QC_nCount_RNA_max & 
                                    percent.mt < QC_percent_mt_max)
```


Set the final singlets to the singlets after filtering by QC cutoffs
```{r Define the final Singlet}
# Define the final Singlet
Sample_final.singlet <- Sample_filtered.singlet
```


Updated Naming Conventions

* This part is specific to sample
```{r HTO- Adding HTO condition to metadata dataframe}
# read in the hashtag to condition file
hashtag_to_condition <- read.csv(Sample_hashtag_to_condition_path)
# create a new metadata column storing the condition information
Sample_final.singlet$condition <- ""

# loop through each row to add the condition label based on hashtag
for (i in 1:nrow(hashtag_to_condition)) {
  row <- hashtag_to_condition[i,]
  # function defined in the Preprocessing_part_1_functions.R file
  Sample_final.singlet <- match_hashtag_to_condition(row, Sample_final.singlet)
}

# Visualize the final table
table(Sample_final.singlet$condition)
```

Finally, save the final singlet Seurat object and RDS object.
```{r save RDS for removed doublets, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(Sample_final.singlet,file = singlets_path)
```



# Summary questions

1. What are the number of cells that are classified as singlets, doublets and negatives respectively and what is the proportions of singlets to all cells? \\
    -> if too many doublets, will consider loading fewer cells in 10X in the future
```{r summary Q1}
# Visualize number of cells per classification (singlets, doublets, negative)
table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)
n_doublet <- table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)[[1]]
n_negative <- table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)[[2]]
n_singlet <- table(Sample$HTO_classification.global)[[3]]
prop_singlet <- n_singlet/(n_doublet + n_negative + n_singlet)
print(paste("The proportion of singlets to total cells is:", prop_singlet))
```

2. What is the proportion of singlets below and above the QC cutoffs (nCounts, nFeatures, percent.mt) to all singlets?  \\
    -> if too high, suggests that this is a low quality sample
```{r summary Q2}
n_QC_singlet <- ncol(Sample_filtered.singlet)
prop_singlet_below_QC <- (n_singlet - n_QC_singlet)/n_singlet
print(paste("The number of singlets after QC is:", n_QC_singlet))
print(paste("The proportion of singlets below and above QC cutoffs to all singlets is:", prop_singlet_below_QC))
```
    
3. What are the number of cells in each conditions?\\
    -> Sanity check (make sure there are no huge differences among conditions)

```{r}
table(Sample_final.singlet$condition)
```



# Preprocessing part 4: Clustering and cell-type labeling

Optional: only if you want to do clustering at the individual sample level

```{r load library for clustering and cell-type labeling}
library(SingleR)
library(celldex)
library(VISION)
```


```{r how to install VISION and SingleR, eval=FALSE}
# how to install VISION
library(devtools)
install_github("YosefLab/VISION")

# downgrading dplyr if celldex/SingleR load dataset doesn't work
devtools::install_version("dbplyr", version = "2.3.4")

#library(BiocManager)
#install("BiocFileCache")
```


```{r load in the sample singlets, eval=FALSE}
# read in the singlets
Sample_final.singlet <- readRDS(file = singlets_path)
```

```{r preprocess the sample singlets, message=FALSE, results='hide'}
# preprocessing
Sample_final.singlet <- FindVariableFeatures(Sample_final.singlet, selection.method = "vst")
Sample_final.singlet <- ScaleData(Sample_final.singlet, features = VariableFeatures(Sample_final.singlet))
Sample_final.singlet <- RunPCA(Sample_final.singlet, features = VariableFeatures(Sample_final.singlet))
Sample_final.singlet <- FindNeighbors(Sample_final.singlet, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:50)
```

```{r clustering, message=FALSE, results='hide'}
# change resolution accordingly
# low resolution -> less clusters; high resolution -> more clusters
Sample_final.singlet <- FindClusters(Sample_final.singlet, resolution = 1.0)
Sample_final.singlet <- RunUMAP(Sample_final.singlet, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:50)
```

```{r umap cluster visualizations}
DimPlot(Sample_final.singlet, reduction = "umap", group.by = "condition", label = FALSE) + ggtitle("by Stim")
DimPlot(Sample_final.singlet, reduction = "umap", group.by = "seurat_clusters", label = FALSE) + ggtitle("by clustering")
```



```{r get DGEs for each cluster, eval=FALSE}
# This step is very time-consuming - ~10 minutes for each cluster
# might need to be run on cluster
gene_markers <- FindAllMarkers(Sample_final.singlet)
```

```{r write out the DEGs for each cluster, eval=FALSE}
# store the DGEs for each cluster separately in a list
list_of_markers <- split(gene_markers, gene_markers$cluster)
# write out the markers
write.xlsx(list_of_markers, file = "clusters_markers.xlsx", rowNames = TRUE)
```

SingleR
```{r SingleR, eval=FALSE}
#Calling on the Monaco Dataset reference
ref <- celldex::MonacoImmuneData()

#ref <- DatabaseImmuneCellExpressionData()

#We use the reference to annotate the clusters we have in our dataset. This identifies marker genes from the reference and uses them to compute assignment scores (based on the Spearman correlation across markers) for each cell in the test dataset against each label in the reference. The label with the highest score is the assigned to the test cell, possibly with further fine-tuning to resolve closely related labels.

#SingleR on a cluster level using the Monaco dataset reference
normalized_count_matrix_immune_population <- GetAssayData(Sample_final.singlet, assay="RNA",slot="data")
immune_populations_labels <- SingleR(test = normalized_count_matrix_immune_population, ref = ref, assay.type.test=1,
    labels = ref$label.fine, clusters=Sample_final.singlet$seurat_clusters)
```

VISION
```{r Run VISION, message=FALSE, results='hide', eval=FALSE}
# create Vision object using the ISG-DC gene signature .gmt file
sig_1 <- c("gene signature .gmt file")
vis_1 <- Vision(Sample_final.singlet, dimRed ="umap", signatures = sig_1, projection_methods = NULL)

#Calculating the signature scores
vis_1 <- analyze(vis_ISG)
```
